originalTitle: Wall Street futures jump after major indexes enter correction territory
summary: Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures jumped on Sunday evening following a bruising week on Wall Street that pushed all three major indexes into correction territory, with technology shares likely to remain in focus during the holiday-shortened trading week.
content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures jumped on Sunday evening following a bruising week on Wall Street that pushed all three major indexes into correction territory, with technology shares likely to remain in focus during the holiday-shortened trading week.

S&P 500 Futures rose 2.2% to 7,090.0 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures surged 2.9% to 25,845.75 points by 20:10 ET (01:10 GMT). Dow Jones Futures climbed 1.6% to 48,964.0 points.

The rebound followed Friday's sharp sell-off, which confirmed that the Dow and S&P 500 had joined the Nasdaq Composite in correction territory, defined as a decline of at least 10% from recent record closing highs.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday to 6,910.39, while the NASDAQ Composite slumped 5.3% to 22,617.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.9% to 48,147.33.

For the week, the Dow dropped about 8%, the S&P 500 shed 8.6%, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 10%, marking some of the steepest weekly losses for the indexes in years. The Nasdaq also slipped into negative territory for 2026.

The selling pressure has been driven largely by growing concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence investment boom, with investors questioning whether the enormous spending on data centres and computing infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.

Concerns intensified following the disappointing performance of Anthropic shares after their high-profile market debut, adding to pressure on technology and semiconductor stocks. Heavyweight Nvidia also came under pressure, amplifying losses across the broader sector.

Investors will now look for signs that last week's decline has run its course or whether further losses lie ahead. Market participants remain divided over whether the correction represents an opportunity to buy beaten-down shares or reflects a deeper reassessment of valuations and corporate earnings prospects.

The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street's fear gauge, closed at 35.89 on Friday, its highest level since the market turmoil triggered by U.S. tariff announcements in April 2025, highlighting elevated investor anxiety.

The economic calendar could also influence trading sentiment. Investors will focus on Wednesday's release of the October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure, for clues about the outlook for monetary policy.

Corporate earnings will provide another test of investor appetite for technology stocks, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Dell Technologies among the companies scheduled to report results during the week.

Trading volumes are expected to be lighter as U.S. markets close on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. Markets will reopen on Friday for a shortened session, with trading scheduled to end at 1 p.m. Eastern time.

The reduced trading schedule could amplify price swings, particularly if investors continue adjusting positions following the recent technology-led sell-off.
